title: Duchy of Luxembourg
capsule: The Duchy of Luxembourg was a Holy Roman Empire fief created in 1354 when Emperor Charles IV elevated his ancestral county to a duchy for his brother Wenceslaus; the Luxembourg dynasty had already produced four Holy Roman Emperors since Henry VII's election in 1308. During the window 1429–1450 the duchy was passing out of Luxembourg hands: Duchess Elizabeth of Görlitz, having pledged the territory to Philip the Good of Burgundy, formally surrendered it in 1443, integrating Luxembourg into the Burgundian Netherlands. The duchy thereafter passed under Habsburg rule through the Burgundian inheritance and remained an imperial fief until the French Revolutionary conquest of 1795.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core territory and the 1443 transfer to Burgundy are well-documented in imperial and Burgundian records; exact extent of peripheral dependencies and forest boundaries in this period carries moderate uncertainty.
